snippets.output: Chlorhexidine is an antiseptic and disinfectant used for skin disinfection before surgery, sterilizing surgical instruments, and various other medical and dental applications.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates properties/uses of chlorhexidine (definition + multiple applications).

snippets.output: Chlorhexidine is effective against a range of microorganisms but does not inactivate spores.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel properties of antimicrobial spectrum (effective against microbes; not against spores).

snippets.output: Chlorhexidine is available in different formulations, including liquid and powder forms, and can be used to disinfect patients’ skin and healthcare providers’ hands.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates formulations and use targets of chlorhexidine.

snippets.output: Chlorhexidine has been used since the 1950s and has a broad spectrum of antiseptic activity.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel attributes (history of use + spectrum) of the same subject.

snippets.output: Chlorhexidine is effective in preventing healthcare-associated infections (HAIs).
snippets.pattern_notes: Single standalone factual claim about HAI prevention.

snippets.output: Chlorhexidine is used for skin cleansing and decolonization, preoperative showering and bathing, vascular catheter site preparation, and oral decontamination.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates clinical use cases of chlorhexidine.

snippets.output: Chlorhexidine has a low risk of causing side effects, but it can cause skin irritation, teeth discoloration, and allergic reactions, with side effects similar to those of other topical antiseptics.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates side-effect profile properties of chlorhexidine.
